<a id="find-purgeable-elements"></a>

### Find purgeable elements

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** which elements of every category are unused in this project or family.

Finds every element Revit counts as unused - in a project or a family, in every category or the ones named - and hands them on for deleting. Version 2 also answers which families are unused, family by family, and on Revit 2020 to 2023 counts placed instances instead - a report that hands nothing on for deleting, because a family nested in another reads as unused. Version 3 also reports, by name, the group definitions with nothing placed, the images nothing uses, the view templates and view filters nothing uses - and, asked for, the materials nothing uses. Only Revit's own list is handed on, and never anything one of those checks finds in use.

| | |

| **Kind** | Answers a question (`READ`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **categories** - text<br>**include materials** - yes or no - true or false; optional |
| **You get** | elements, purgeable names, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |
| **Capability** | `FIND_PURGEABLE_ELEMENTS` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"list everything purgeable in this family"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
3. Heron answers in the chat. Nothing in the model changes.

Other ways to ask: *"every unused element, all categories"* · *"find the unused elements of every category in the model"*

<a id="pick-on-screen"></a>

### Pick on screen

**DRAFT - runs in a chat, and its answer says so.** It changes nothing in the model, so it is not refused, but it has not been proved on a real model yet.

**What it does:** ask the modeller to click a point in the open Revit view and hand it back in millimetres.

Waits for the modeller to click one point in the Revit view in front and hands it back in millimetres, written the way a point is typed everywhere else in this library, so the next step can take it as it is. Esc cancels. Changes nothing in the model. One point for each time it is asked. Revit waits for the click for several minutes; tell the modeller before asking, and if Heron reports it stopped waiting for the click, tell them to press Esc in Revit and ask again once they are ready at Revit.

<a id="read-selection"></a>

### Read selection

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-13 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** what has the user already picked on screen, right now.

Reads what the user has selected in Revit and hands it on as `elements`. **It is the other half of the library.** Every filter here starts from a described set - a category, a type, a room, an id. This one starts from the set a human already pointed at, which is how a modeller works most of the time: pick the four ducts on screen, then say what to do to them. Without it, *"move these up 200"* has no "these", and the whole library can only act on what it can describe in words. **It is a READ, and that is the point of it existing separately.** SET_SELECTION writes the selection; this one only looks at it. Before this fragment, *"what did I select"* resolved to SET_SELECTION - a question answered by the fragment that CHANGES the thing being asked about, which is the worst kind of wrong answer because it looks plausible and is destructive.

<a id="select-by-connector-size"></a>

### Select by connector size

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-08 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** the ones whose connector is actually 230 by 230, not the ones whose name says so.

Keeps the elements that have a CONNECTOR of the size asked for, measured off the connector itself. It changes nothing. **A PARAMETER FILTER CANNOT ASK THIS QUESTION.** Size parameters describe the duct or the pipe; a connector is where it JOINS, and on a piece of equipment those are different numbers. An AHU whose type is called `AHU-01` has a supply connector of some size, and nothing in its parameters is that size. Filtering on a name is filtering on what somebody typed. **MILLIMETRES IN, FEET INSIDE.** Revit stores connector dimensions in decimal feet. The sizes here are given in **millimetres**, because that is what a drawing says, and are converted once at 304.8 mm per foot. A tolerance is required rather than optional: 230 mm is 0.75459... feet and no stored value will equal a typed one exactly. **ORIENTATION IS A POLICY, NOT A DETAIL.** A 400 x 230 duct and a 230 x 400 duct are the same duct rotated. Whether that counts as a match is the caller's decision, so it is a flag - and it defaults to matching either way round, because that is what somebody asking for "230 by 400" almost always means. **AN ELEMENT MATCHES IF ANY ONE OF ITS CONNECTORS MATCHES.** A fitting has several and they differ; requiring all of them would return nothing on every reducer, which is the fitting most worth finding. **THREE OUTCOMES, NOT TWO.** Matched, and then two kinds of miss that are not the same thing: an element with NO connectors at all (a wall, a generic model - the filter has nothing to measure) and an element whose connector shape is one this cannot measure. Merging them into "did not match" would hide a wrong selection behind a plausible number. Reads only. Opens no transaction and needs none.

<a id="select-by-design-option"></a>

### Select by design option

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-08 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** the elements inside one design option, or the ones in none.

Narrows the model to the elements belonging to ONE named design option - "show me what is in Scheme B" - or, with no option named, to the elements in no option at all, which is the Main Model. **TWO DESIGN OPTIONS CAN HAVE THE SAME NAME, AND THAT IS THE NORMAL CASE.** Revit names the primary option of EVERY option set "Option 1 (primary)", so a model with three option sets has three options called exactly that. A lookup that takes the first match picks whichever the collector returned first and reports success - the wrong answer delivered with confidence, which is the defect this whole project is built around. **This refuses to choose.** When a name is ambiguous it names the option sets involved and stops, so the caller can say which set they meant. **"No option" means the Main Model, and it is almost the whole file.** An unbounded Main Model sweep returns nearly every element in the project. Give a category list unless the whole model is genuinely wanted. **An element in the OTHER option of the same set is not "missing".** Design options are alternatives, so what is not in the option asked for is in a sibling option or in the Main Model. A count smaller than expected usually means the elements are in the sibling, not that they were dropped. **A model with no design options at all is answered, not refused.** Unlike an unworkshared model asked about worksets, "there are no design options" and "the Main Model is everything" are the same true statement, and the Main Model answer is still correct. Only a NAMED option that does not exist is refused.

| **You get** | elements, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |
| **Capability** | `SELECT_BY_DESIGN_OPTION` |

3. Heron answers in the chat. Nothing in the model changes.

<a id="select-by-host"></a>

### Select by host

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** the doors, windows and other things really hosted in this wall or element, not the things near it.

Finds the doors and windows already cut into a wall - selects them, and counts them - and everything else Revit records as HOSTED ON one given element: the skylights in a roof, the face-hosted fixtures on a ceiling, the insulation and lining wrapped around a duct or pipe. The answer is the selection, with a count beside it of every door, window and other family found on it and of the insulation wraps, narrowed to Doors or Windows when the category is given. One host per call. **A read, never a change.** It finds each door and window a wall already has; adding a new one is a different tool, and nothing here edits the wall. **This is the recorded parent relationship, not proximity.** Two elements touching, overlapping or sharing a face do not host one another, and nothing here will find them. That is the point: a host relationship is what makes the child move when the parent moves, and it is the only one worth filtering on when the question is "what depends on this". Two mechanisms are covered, because Revit uses two and neither one alone is enough: `FamilyInstance.Host` for a door, a window and every other host-based family, and `InsulationLiningBase.HostElementId` for insulation and lining. A filter that reads only the first finds no insulation at all and says so with a confident zero. **MEP FITTINGS ARE CONNECTED TO THEIR RUN, AND THE RUN IS NOT THEIR HOST.** An elbow, a tee or a valve has connectors and NO host, so "what is on this pipe" comes back empty here - correct, and useless. TRACE_CONNECTIVITY follows connectors and answers it, and the empty result says so in words. **A level is not a host in this sense either.** Almost every element records a level, so "everything on Level 2" is a different question - FILTER_ELEMENTS_BY_CATEGORY takes a level and answers it.

| **You get** | elements, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2020 |
| **Capability** | `SELECT_BY_HOST` |

**How to use it**

2. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"how many doors are hosted in these walls"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.

<a id="select-by-material"></a>

### Select by material

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-13 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** the elements made of one material.

Narrows the model to the elements that use one named material - "which walls are fair-faced block", "everything in galvanised steel" - optionally bounded to a list of categories. **Revit has no material-to-elements lookup, so this is a SCAN and says so.** Every element in scope is asked what it is made of; there is no index to consult. That is not an implementation detail the caller can ignore - it is why the category bound matters here more than in most filters, and why the scanned count is reported beside the answer. **Paint is a separate question and is off by default.** A material can reach an element two ways: as its real make-up, through the type's compound structure or family geometry, or as PAINT applied to one face. "What is this wall made of" and "what did we paint" are different questions with different answers, and folding them together silently would inflate the first. Asking for paint includes both, and the report says which was asked. **A material name that does not exist is refused, with the real names listed.** Revit material names are long, near-duplicated and inconsistently punctuated - "Steel, Galvanized" against "Steel - Galvanized" - so a miss is far more often a spelling than an absence, and a bare zero would read as the wrong one. **The material usually lives on the TYPE, and that is not a mistake.** An instance reports the materials its type and geometry give it, so every wall of one type answers alike. Changing what one is made of means a new type, which is DUPLICATE_TYPE and then REPLACE_MATERIAL. **LINKED MODELS ARE READ ONLY WHEN ASKED FOR (version 2, D-59).** With `includeLinks` absent this answers for this model alone, exactly as the proof measured. With it set, every loaded link is read too and `linksSearched` says how many were: set and 0 means "you asked, and none are loaded", which is a different answer from host-only. The material is looked for BY NAME in each link - the architect's materials are usually only there - and each link's count, or "no material called", is in `linkedMatches`. **NOTHING FROM A LINK IS EVER SELECTED OR CARRIED** - `elements` stays this model's own; the chain revives ids against this model, and a linked id that happens to be in use here binds an unrelated element (FRAGMENT-ISSUES row 75). Links nested inside a link are not read, and are counted in the answer. **IN A FAMILY OPEN IN THE FAMILY EDITOR, EVERY FORM IS SCANNED (version 3).** A form there carries no category of its own - measured 2026-10-08 in Revit 2024, its category is empty, or is its subcategory - so a category list never reached one, and "Generic Models" in a Generic Model family scanned 0 of 0. Now every extrusion, revolve, blend, sweep, swept blend and freeform solid is asked what it is made of whatever the list says, and the list still bounds the rest of the family. A form whose material is <By Category> names none, and the answer counts those. The forms found go on to SET_SELECTION or DELETE_ELEMENTS like any other.

| **You get** | elements, findings |

<a id="select-by-parameter-value"></a>

### Select by parameter value

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** the elements whose parameter text matches what i typed.

Selects the elements of one TYPE by its name, or whose named parameter matches a piece of TEXT - "every curtain wall of type Atrium Glass", "every door of type Office Single", "every VCD", "mark begins with AHU" - optionally bounded to a list of categories. Three names are understood beyond real parameters, because they are what a modeller actually says: **Family**, **Type**, and **Family and Type**. The last one matches against `Family : Type` the way Revit's own properties palette writes it - "Curtain Wall : Storefront". So "select every curtain wall of type Storefront" is Type equals Storefront, in Walls. **One element picked by its own name is Name equals that text**, in its category: "select the level called Ground" is Name equals Ground, in Levels, and a grid named B is Name equals B, in Grids (row 5b-1951). **AN ELEMENT THAT DOES NOT CARRY THE PARAMETER IS COUNTED, NEVER MATCHED - not even by a "does not contain" query.** Treating a missing parameter as an empty string is the obvious code and it is wrong in one direction that matters: "everything whose Mark is not ABC" then returns every element in the model, including the thousands that have no Mark at all. They are reported as `withoutParameter` instead, which also means a MISTYPED parameter name comes back as "0 matched, 4,812 do not carry it" rather than as a plausible zero. **A text mode matches text, and a number is not text.** A length, an airflow or a pressure is stored as a double and only becomes "500" after Revit formats it - in the project's display units, with the project's rounding and separators. Searching for "500" as text finds it in a millimetre project, misses it in a metre one, and misses 500.4 rounded to "500" in neither predictably. The NUMERIC modes compare the stored number instead, and are the right answer for anything with a unit. **Type parameters are searched after instance parameters, and only if asked.** A name that exists on both wins at the instance, which is the same order Revit's own schedules use. **LINKED MODELS ARE READ ONLY WHEN ASKED FOR (version 2, D-59).** With `includeLinks` absent this answers for this model alone, exactly as the proof measured. With it set, every loaded link is read too and `linksSearched` says how many were: set and 0 means "you asked, and none are loaded", which is a different answer from host-only. The same match runs in each link and its matches are counted per link in `linkedMatches`. **NOTHING FROM A LINK IS EVER SELECTED OR CARRIED** - `elements` stays this model's own; the chain revives ids against this model, and a linked id that happens to be in use here binds an unrelated element (FRAGMENT-ISSUES row 75). Links nested inside a link are not read, and are counted in the answer. **VERSION 4 ALSO FINDS BY FAMILY AND COMPARES NUMBERS** - SELECT_BY_FAMILY and SELECT_BY_NUMERIC_PARAMETER were merged in. Family as the parameter finds every element of a named family wherever it is, the category optional, `exactMatch` for one family whose name another contains; the families that matched are counted in `matchedFamilies` and an unbounded sweep is said in `scannedWholeModel`. Modes gt, gte, lt, lte, between, eq and ne compare a stored number - "ducts 500 mm high", "pipes larger than 100" - with `compareValue` in Revit's internal unit (500 mm is 500/304.8), eq to a tolerance, and a parameter held as text is counted in `notNumeric`.

<a id="select-by-phase"></a>

### Select by phase

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** the elements created in one phase, or demolished in one.

Narrows the model to the elements whose Phase Created, or Phase Demolished, is one named project phase - "everything added in Phase 2", "what is coming out in Phase 1" - optionally bounded to a list of categories. Both may be asked at once, and then both must hold. **MOST OF A MODEL HAS NO PHASING AT ALL, and that is counted rather than dropped.** Levels, grids, views, sheets, view-specific annotation and every element type carry no phase parameters. The obvious code swallows them in a try/catch and reports only the matches, so a broken phase lookup and a correct small answer read identically. This reports `withoutPhasing` alongside, exactly as FILTER_ELEMENTS_BY_CATEGORY reports `unresolvedLevel` and for the same reason: a thing that does nothing must never be able to look like a thing that worked. **Phase is read from `CreatedPhaseId` and `DemolishedPhaseId`, and those were checked on 2020 rather than assumed.** The obvious guess is that a property pair this readable arrived later than 2020 and that the two phase BuiltInParameters are the safe route; a compile on both ends of the range says otherwise, and the guess would have put a false sentence in this file. **"Demolished in Phase 1" is not "demolished".** An element that is never demolished has no demolition phase at all, so asking for a named one answers a narrower question than it sounds like. Say which phase, or ask a different question. **A phase name that does not exist is refused, with the real names listed.** Revit's default phases are "Existing" and "New Construction" and almost every office renames them; a typo must not come back as an empty phase. **LINKED MODELS ARE READ ONLY WHEN ASKED FOR (version 2, D-59).** With `includeLinks` absent this answers for this model alone, exactly as the proof measured. With it set, every loaded link is read too and `linksSearched` says how many were: set and 0 means "you asked, and none are loaded", which is a different answer from host-only. Each link is asked for the phases BY NAME and its matches are counted per link in `linkedMatches`, or the link says it has no phase of that name. **NOTHING FROM A LINK IS EVER SELECTED OR CARRIED** - `elements` stays this model's own; the chain revives ids against this model, and a linked id that happens to be in use here binds an unrelated element (FRAGMENT-ISSUES row 75). Links nested inside a link are not read, and are counted in the answer. This is version 2; version 1's proof no longer describes the code, and the fragment is DRAFT until it is proved again.

| | |
|---|---|

<a id="select-by-pin-state"></a>

### Select by pin state

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-08 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** the elements that are pinned, or the ones that are not.

Narrows the model to the elements that ARE pinned, or to the ones that are NOT, optionally bounded to a list of categories. It is the read half of the pair SET_PIN_STATE writes, and it is the sweep that answers "what did we actually lock down" before a big move. **Asked over the whole model, "everything pinned" is mostly links and datums.** Revit pins a linked model and an imported CAD file when it is inserted, and most teams pin their grids and levels early. So an unbounded answer is dominated by things nobody was asking about, and the category bound is what makes the question the one that was meant. The report says which case it just answered. **The unpinned sweep is the more useful one, and it is the bigger one.** "Which grids are NOT pinned" is a real check with a short answer; "which elements are not pinned" is almost the entire model. Both are offered because the first is worth having, and the count is reported beside the scan size so the second cannot be mistaken for a finding. **A pinned group and its members are separate facts.** Pinning a group instance does not pin what is inside it, and this reports exactly what each element says about itself. Reports how many elements were scanned as well as how many matched, so a small answer can be read against the size of the sweep.

<a id="select-by-workset"></a>

### Select by workset

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-08 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** the elements that sit on one named workset.

Narrows the model to the elements on ONE named user workset, optionally bounded to a list of categories. It is the "show me what is on Linked Models" / "what did the structural team put on their workset" question, and it is the set almost every workset clean-up starts from. **A model that is not workshared has no worksets, and that is a REFUSAL rather than an empty answer.** The two look identical from the outside - zero elements - and they mean opposite things. One says "nothing is on that workset"; the other says "the question does not apply to this file". A filter that returns a confident zero for the second is the exact defect this project exists around. **A workset name that does not exist is also a refusal, and the existing names are listed.** Typing `Linked models` for `Linked Models` must not read as "that workset is empty". The names are given back so the next attempt is a correction rather than a guess. **Only USER worksets are searched.** A workshared model also carries family worksets and view worksets, which Revit maintains and nobody assigns work to. A modeller asking about "the MEP workset" means the user one, and matching across all kinds would let an internal name win. **This says nothing about who OWNS or has CHECKED OUT those elements.** Workset is where an element lives; ownership is who is holding it right now. They are different questions and REPORT_ELEMENT_OWNERSHIP answers the second. Reports how many elements were scanned as well as how many matched, so a small answer can be read against the size of the sweep.

<a id="select-from-link"></a>

### Select from link

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-08 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** the elements inside a linked model, not the link itself.

Reaches inside a loaded Revit link and returns the elements in it - "how many beams are in the structural model", "what ducts does the MEP link have" - bounded to a list of categories. **WHAT COMES BACK BELONGS TO ANOTHER DOCUMENT, AND ALMOST EVERY ACTION IN THIS LIBRARY WILL FAIL ON IT.** These elements live in the linked file, not the host. Their ids resolve only inside that file, so a fragment that calls `doc.GetElement(element.Id)` gets the wrong element or nothing at all - and nothing can be written into a link from the host session in any case. They are safe to READ: name, category, parameters, geometry, all read straight off the object. They are not safe to move, set, tag or delete. This is stated here, where the set is produced, because the failure downstream is silent or worse. **The link's geometry is in the link's own coordinates.** Where a link was placed with an offset or a rotation, a point read off one of these elements is not a point in the host model until the link's transform is applied. Any distance or clash reasoning across the boundary has to do that; this fragment returns the elements and does not move them. **An unloaded link is a refusal, not an empty answer.** A link that is present but unloaded has no document to read, and zero elements would read as "the structural model is empty" rather than "nobody loaded it". **A name that matches nothing is refused with the loaded links listed**, and a name that matches several is refused rather than guessed - a project with two structural links has two right answers and no way to choose between them.

<a id="select-from-saved-set"></a>

### Select from saved set

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-13 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** what is actually in that filter i saved earlier.

Reads a named filter back out as a set of elements - the other half of UPDATE_SAVED_SET, which saves a set and could not until now get it back, and of CREATE_VIEW_FILTER, which writes a rule. **The two kinds of filter are the same word and two different things, and this fragment is where that finally bites.** A **selection filter** stores an explicit list of ids: reading it means handing back what was saved, and the answer is the same in every view. A **view filter** stores a RULE - everything whose System Type contains CHW - and there is no list to read. "Its elements" can only mean *the elements that rule matches, in one view*, so a view must be named, and the same rule in a different view is a different answer. **So a view filter without a view is refused, not guessed.** Falling back to the active view would answer a question about whichever drawing happened to be open, and would be right often enough that nobody would notice when it was not. **A saved list can hold ids that no longer exist**, because deleting an element does not tidy the sets that mentioned it. Those are counted as `missing` rather than dropped, which is the difference between "the set has shrunk" and "the set was always this size". **A name that matches nothing is refused with the real names listed**, and the report says which kind each filter is - the thing you have to know before you can ask this question properly.

<a id="select-group-members"></a>

### Select group members

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** everything inside this group or assembly, as elements i can act on.

Returns the member elements of a model group instance - the repeated toilet block, the typical FCU-and-terminals cluster - or of an assembly - the pipe spool, the prefabricated riser - as a set the next fragment can act on. **An assembly is opened the same way, and says it is one.** Version 2. An assembly (Create > Assembly) is a container of its own: like a group, the collector returns the assembly and not its members, and like a group it is opened by the instance, never by a name several copies share. Its members are read back with the assembly's type name and naming category, and `containerKind` says which of the two was opened. **A group instance is one element, and its members are not in any normal sweep.** `FilteredElementCollector` returns the group, not the twelve things inside it, so every count and every filter in this library sees a group as a single item. This is the fragment that opens it. **Reading a group is safe; acting on what comes out usually is not.** Revit will not let a member be changed in place - editing one means entering group edit mode, or the change applies to every instance of that group type. So this returns the members and says plainly that a write against them is likely to be refused or to hit every copy. That warning belongs here, at the point the set is produced, not at the point somebody is surprised. **A group NAME is a type name, and several instances share it.** Naming a group by name is therefore ambiguous whenever it is placed more than once - which is the entire reason groups exist. So an instance is what this takes, and there is no name lookup to guess with. **Nested groups come back as groups**, one element each, not flattened. A member that is itself a group can be handed back in for its own members; flattening silently would make the count disagree with what Revit shows and hide a structure the modeller built on purpose. **A FAMILY INSTANCE IS OPENED TOO** (version 3) - its nested shared families, the parts a category sweep never returns: the fan and coil inside an air handling unit. Nesting goes as deep as somebody built it, so it is followed by default and the depth is reported; a parent with no sub-components is the ordinary case and is counted, never mistaken for a failed read.

<a id="select-in-region"></a>

### Select in region

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** everything inside this box of space.

Narrows the model to the elements that TOUCH a rectangular volume given by two corners - inside it or crossing its edge - the "what is in this area" question when there is no room to filter by, or the area crosses several rooms, or it is outdoors. **TOUCHING, NOT CONTAINED.** Both tests are intersect tests, so an element only partly in the box counts. A box just bigger than an element proves it touches the box, never that it sits inside it: to measure a gap, use two strips, one stopping short that returns nothing and one reaching past that returns it (row 5b-193 - a 602 mm box around a 600 mm diffuser was once read as "centred within 1 mm"). **Two tests, one fragment, and the caller says which.** The fast test asks whether an element's BOUNDING BOX overlaps the volume. The exact test asks whether its real geometry does. They were two files in the earlier library and they answer one question at two accuracies, which is a flag rather than a second fragment - the same call CREATE_MEP_RUNS makes about tray and conduit. **The difference is not academic and the report always names which ran.** A bounding box is axis-aligned, so a sloped drainage pipe or a rotated duct has a box far larger than the pipe: it is reported as inside a volume it never enters. On level work the two agree; on anything sloped or rotated the fast test OVER-reports, and silently. **The exact test is slower and it is not free of its own trap:** an element with no solid geometry at all - many annotation and analytical elements - cannot intersect anything and drops out. Those are counted rather than dropped, so a small exact answer beside a large fast one can be read. **Corners are typed in millimetres and arrive here ALREADY IN FEET.** The add-in's point parser converts every XYZ with HeronUnits.MillimetresToFeet before a fragment sees it, because Revit's internal unit is the foot. This fragment converted a SECOND time until 2026-09-13, which divided every region by 304.8 - a 200 m box became a 656 mm one and the answer was a calm "0 element(s)". 304.8 now appears once, turning feet back into the millimetres the report speaks.** Nothing about this needs a units API, and the report states the volume in millimetres so a value handed in already converted shows up as an absurd box rather than as a quiet zero. **The two corners are sorted, so either order works.** A volume given max-first is not an error a modeller should have to think about. **LINKED MODELS ARE READ ONLY WHEN ASKED FOR (version 2, D-59).** With `includeLinks` absent this answers for this model alone, exactly as the proof measured. With it set, every loaded link is read too and `linksSearched` says how many were: set and 0 means "you asked, and none are loaded", which is a different answer from host-only. The same volume is moved into each link through each placement's transform, and the matches are counted per link in `linkedMatches`. **NOTHING FROM A LINK IS EVER SELECTED OR CARRIED** - `elements` stays this model's own; the chain revives ids against this model, and a linked id that happens to be in use here binds an unrelated element (FRAGMENT-ISSUES row 75). Links nested inside a link are not read, and are counted in the answer.

<a id="select-openings"></a>

### Select openings

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** where are the shafts and the holes in the slab.

Collects the openings cut through the building - shafts, floor openings, wall openings, roof openings - as a set to act on. The MEP question behind it is always the same: where can this riser go, and is there a hole here already. **ONE QUERY MISSES MOST OF THEM, BECAUSE OPENINGS ARE NOT ONE CATEGORY.** They are spread across several - a shaft cutting many levels, a hole in a slab, a rectangular opening in a wall, one in a roof - and each is its own category with its own name. Asking for the obvious one comes back with a fraction of what is there and looks like an answer. **AN OPENING CUT BY A FAMILY IS NOT AN OPENING ELEMENT.** The hole a door or a window makes belongs to that family and appears in none of these categories. That is correct - it is the door's hole, not a shaft - and it is said here because "show me every hole" means both to a person, and only one of them is findable this way. **THE BREAKDOWN IS PART OF THE ANSWER.** Twelve shafts is a coordination picture; twelve floor openings is a different one. They are counted per kind rather than summed. ASSUMES NOTHING ABOUT TRANSACTIONS - it opens none and needs none. **LINKED MODELS ARE READ ONLY WHEN ASKED FOR (version 2, D-59).** With `includeLinks` absent this answers for this model alone, exactly as version 1 did. With it set, every loaded link is read too and `linksSearched` says how many were: set and 0 means "you asked, and none are loaded", which is a different answer from host-only. Each link's shafts and slab, wall, roof and column openings are counted per link and per kind in `linkedMatches` - for MEP coordination they are usually in a link; with a view, through that view, which only Revit 2023 and later can do. **NOTHING FROM A LINK IS EVER SELECTED OR CARRIED** - `elements` and `byKind` stay this model's own; the chain revives ids against this model, and a linked id that happens to be in use here binds an unrelated element (FRAGMENT-ISSUES row 75). Links nested inside a link are not read, and are counted in the answer.

<a id="select-scope-boxes"></a>

### Select scope boxes

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** give me the scope boxes themselves as a set I can act on.

Returns the Scope Boxes in the model as elements, narrowed by name - and, for one box, its corners. **EVERYTHING ELSE HERE TAKES A SCOPE BOX BY NAME, AND THAT IS THE GAP.** ASSIGN_SCOPE_BOX_TO_VIEW puts a named one onto views, and until version 2 READ_SCOPE_BOX_EXTENT found one by name and handed back its corners. Neither could answer *"what scope boxes are there"*, and neither could hand a set to a rename, a report or a delete. A scope box is an ordinary element and nothing here could reach it as one. This is the same shape as the gap SELECT_VIEW_TEMPLATES filled, found the same way. **A SCOPE BOX CANNOT BE CREATED FROM CODE, WHICH MAKES REACHING THE EXISTING ONES MORE USEFUL, NOT LESS.** Revit exposes no create call on any release here - every box is drawn once by hand - so the ones in the model are all there will ever be, and renaming or auditing them is the only automation available. Resizing one is out too: the delete-and-recreate route needs the create call that does not exist. **IT IS FOUND BY CATEGORY, NOT BY CLASS.** A scope box has no dedicated API class - it is an ordinary element in the Volume of Interest category, which is why a class-based query finds nothing and why the earlier library reached it by category as well. A search for a Scope Box type is the most likely wrong turn here. **VERSION 2 ALSO SAYS HOW BIG ONE BOX IS, AND WHERE** (READ_SCOPE_BOX_EXTENT merged in): with one box matching, its two corners in millimetres - minMm and maxMm, the names SELECT_IN_REGION takes, so *"what is inside the podium scope box"* composes with nothing in between - and its id. Asked for an extent with two boxes matching, it refuses rather than picking one: they are usually different halves of a building. ASSUMES NOTHING ABOUT TRANSACTIONS - it opens none and needs none.

<a id="select-types"></a>

### Select types

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-19 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** give me the types themselves, not the things placed from them.

Returns the TYPE elements themselves - a family type, a duct type, a pipe type, a wall type - narrowed by category, by family name and by type name. Not the instances placed from them. **A TYPE WITH NOTHING PLACED IS OTHERWISE UNREACHABLE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS EXISTS.** Every other route to a type in this library starts from an element and asks what type it is: FILTER_ELEMENTS_BY_TYPE takes an exemplar, CHANGE_ELEMENT_TYPE and DUPLICATE_TYPE both resolve from instances. All of them are blind to a type that has been loaded and never used - which is exactly the type somebody wants to rename before it spreads, or purge, or check against a naming standard. Starting from the instances cannot see it, by construction. **A TYPE IS AN ELEMENT AND CAN BE ACTED ON LIKE ONE.** That is not obvious and it is the point of returning `elements` rather than a list of names: a type can be renamed, have parameters written to it, be reported on, be deleted. Handing back strings would make this a report and stop it composing with everything that takes elements. **CATEGORIES ARE RESOLVED CATEGORIES, NEVER NAMES IN A STRING.** Turning a BIM word into a category is its own job and belongs upstream; a fragment that accepted "duct accessory" would be guessing at somebody else's vocabulary. Passing none means every category, which is the honest answer to "list the types in this model" and is deliberately allowed. **FAMILY NAME MEANS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND BOTH ARE ANSWERED.** A loadable family type carries its family as an object; a system family type - duct, pipe, wall - carries only a family NAME, and asking it for a family object gets nothing. Matching one way and not the other is how a filter reports zero for a duct type whose family is sitting there in the browser. **IT COUNTS NOTHING AND JUDGES NOTHING.** *"Which types are unused"* is FIND_PURGEABLE_ELEMENTS, which asks Revit's unused list to prove it. This one hands back the types that match a description and leaves the judgement alone.

<a id="select-unenclosed-rooms"></a>

### Select unenclosed rooms

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** find the rooms that are not enclosed or were never placed.

Sweeps the model for Rooms and MEP Spaces that are not doing their job - placed where the boundaries do not close, or never placed at all - and hands them on as the set to act on. Read-only. Areas too, when asked (version 3). **THE TWO FAULTS LOOK IDENTICAL AND NEED OPPOSITE FIXES.** Both report zero area. A room with no location was never put in the model: it sits in the schedule and is deleted or placed. A room with a location and no area was placed somewhere its boundaries do not close: a wall, a gap, or a room-bounding setting. Reporting them as one list of "bad rooms" sends somebody looking for walls around a room that is not in the model. **AN UNBOUNDED SPACE IS AN MEP PROBLEM, NOT A TIDINESS ONE.** A Space with no volume carries no heating or cooling load, and it is still in the schedule with zeros in it. The load calculation completes, the numbers look like numbers, and the room is simply missing from the total. **REDUNDANCY IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE.** Two rooms in one enclosed region is a third fault and Revit already reports it as a warning, which `READ_MODEL_WARNINGS` reads. Re-deriving it from geometry here would be a second, weaker answer to a question already answered properly. The faulty elements are handed on as `elements`, which is the pipeline's currency - the name the next action consumes - with the two states also named separately so the report can say which fix each one needs. ASSUMES NOTHING ABOUT TRANSACTIONS - it opens none and needs none. **LINKED MODELS ARE READ ONLY WHEN ASKED FOR (version 2, D-59).** With `includeLinks` absent this answers for this model alone, exactly as the proof measured. With it set, every loaded link is read too and `linksSearched` says how many were: set and 0 means "you asked, and none are loaded", which is a different answer from host-only. Each link's unplaced and unenclosed rooms or spaces are listed by name in `linkedMatches`. On an MEP model the rooms are usually in the architectural link, so this is where it matters. **NOTHING FROM A LINK IS EVER SELECTED OR CARRIED** - `elements`, `unplaced` and `unenclosed` stay this model's own; the chain revives ids against this model, and a linked id that happens to be in use here binds an unrelated element (FRAGMENT-ISSUES row 75). Links nested inside a link are not read, and are counted in the answer.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Answers a question (`READ`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **include rooms** - yes or no - true or false<br>**include spaces** - yes or no - true or false<br>**include areas** - yes or no - true or false; optional<br>**include links** - yes or no - true or false; optional |
| **You get** | elements, unplaced, unenclosed |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2020 |
| **Capability** | `SELECT_UNENCLOSED_ROOMS` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"which rooms are not enclosed"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
3. Heron answers in the chat. Nothing in the model changes.

Other ways to ask: *"find the unbounded spaces"* · *"rooms with no area"*

<a id="select-view-templates"></a>

### Select view templates

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-09 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** give me the view templates themselves as a set I can act on.

Returns the View Templates themselves as elements, narrowed by name and by whether anything uses them. Not the views that follow them. **EVERY OTHER TEMPLATE FRAGMENT HERE TAKES A TEMPLATE BY NAME, AND THAT IS THE GAP.** APPLY_VIEW_TEMPLATE, REMOVE_VIEW_TEMPLATE, DUPLICATE_VIEWS and SET_VIEW_TEMPLATE_CONTROL all start from a template somebody has already named. None of them can answer *"do it to all of them"*, or hand a set of templates to a rename, a report or a delete. A template is an element like any other and nothing here could reach it as one. **USED AND UNUSED ARE NOT THE SAME QUESTION AS APPLIED AND NOT APPLIED, AND GETTING THAT WRONG DELETES A LIVE TEMPLATE.** A template is in use if a view follows it - and ALSO if a view family type names it as the template new views of that kind start with. The second is invisible: no view points at it, so a check that only walks views calls it unused, and deleting it silently changes what every new plan is created with. Both reasons are gathered, and both are reported per template rather than collapsed into one flag. **AN UNRECOGNISED USAGE MODE RETURNS NOTHING, NOT EVERYTHING.** A typo in the mode falling back to "no filter" hands the whole template list to whatever comes next, and what comes next is often a delete. The refusal is reported as a finding. **IT DELETES NOTHING AND JUDGES NOTHING.** *"Which definitions is nobody using"* as a report is FIND_PURGEABLE_ELEMENTS (FIND_UNUSED_DEFINITIONS until it was merged in, 2026-11-01), which also covers view filters and states its own reasoning about them. This one hands back templates as elements so something else can act, which is the half that was missing. **BUILDING IT FOUND A DEFECT IN THAT ONE.** FIND_UNUSED_DEFINITIONS walked views only, so a template used solely as a view family type's default was reported unused. Asking the same question a third way is what made the two answers disagree, and it was corrected the same day. Both now check both kinds of use. ASSUMES NOTHING ABOUT TRANSACTIONS - it opens none and needs none.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Answers a question (`READ`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **name contains** - text<br>**usage** - text |
| **You get** | elements, matched names, findings, found |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |
| **Capability** | `SELECT_VIEW_TEMPLATES` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"give me the view templates"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
3. Heron answers in the chat. Nothing in the model changes.

<a id="set-selection"></a>

### Set selection

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** put these elements in the current selection.

Answers "what to do to them" for the commonest read-only job there is: show the user what was found, on screen, where they can see it. Pairs with any filter - that is the point of it being a separate fragment rather than part of a "select ducts" whole. **VERSION 2 ALSO TAKES YOU TO THEM** (ZOOM_TO_ELEMENTS merged in). Selecting is not showing: with show, Revit's own Show moves the screen to the elements - and may change the active view, so the view it landed on comes back in viewAfter. With keepSelection too, the camera moves and the selection is left alone - "where is it". Ids that no longer exist are left out and named in missing.

<a id="update-saved-set"></a>

### Update saved set

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-14 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** add these to the set i saved, or take them out of it.

Changes what is in a named selection set that already exists - adds elements, removes them, replaces the lot, or deletes the set. The other half of saving a set: parking the beams while the ducts are run is only useful if the parked set can be corrected afterwards. **THE SET LIVES IN THE MODEL, NOT IN THIS SESSION.** It is a real element, so it survives the file being closed, it is visible to everybody on the job, and Revit maintains it as elements are deleted. That is also why editing one is a model change with an undo entry, not a convenience. **IDS IN THE SET THAT NO LONGER RESOLVE ARE COUNTED, NEVER SILENTLY DROPPED.** A saved set outlives the elements in it. Somebody deletes forty beams, the set still names them, and a set that quietly shrinks looks like it was edited by somebody. `missing` is that number, read fresh each time. **CREATING IS ASKED FOR BY NAME, WITH MODE "create" (version 2).** Asking to add to a set that does not exist is almost always the name being wrong - spelled differently, or on another model - so it is still refused. Creating one silently would leave two sets a letter apart, both half right. Mode "create" saves the elements as a new set, read back, applied to no view; a name already in use is refused and points at "replace". ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

| **Works on** | what is selected in Revit: elements |
| **You say** | **set name** - text<br>**mode** - text |
| **You get** | set size, changed, deleted, filter id, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2020 |
| **Capability** | `UPDATE_SAVED_SET` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. Select what it works on in Revit (elements) - or name it in the same request, and Heron finds it first.
3. Turn **Changes** on in Heron's **Settings** (Heron tab).
4. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"add these to the saved set"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
5. Heron makes the change as **one entry in Revit's Undo list**. With **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** first; Ctrl+Z takes it back.

<a id="zoom-to-linked-elements"></a>

### Zoom to linked elements

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** take me to these elements in the linked model, on screen.

Zooms the active view to elements INSIDE A LOADED REVIT LINK - "zoom to the beams in the structural link" - and, when asked, selects them as linked elements, so the person can see what SELECT_FROM_LINK found. **SET_SELECTION'S SHOW CANNOT DO THIS, AND THE REASON IS THE WHOLE FRAGMENT.** Revit's Show takes ids in the host document, and a linked element's id means nothing there - or names an unrelated host element that shares the number. So the boxes are read off the linked elements, put through the link's own transform into host coordinates, and the active view is zoomed to the box round all of them with `UIView.ZoomAndCenterRectangle`. All eight corners of each box are transformed, because once a link is rotated the far corner in the link is not the far corner in the host. **IT ZOOMS THE VIEW ON SCREEN AND NEVER JUMPS TO ANOTHER.** Show picks a view; nothing in Revit finds a view that shows a linked element, so a sheet, a schedule, a legend or a drafting view is refused by name. Whether each element is DRAWN once the camera is there is the view's - its crop, its view range or section box, and its visibility settings for the link - and the answer says so. **SELECTING INSIDE A LINK NEEDS REVIT 2023 OR LATER.** `Selection.SetReferences` arrived at 2023, so it is looked up by reflection when `alsoSelect` is true and one source compiles on every release. On 2020 to 2022 the camera still moves and a finding says the selection could not be set. The references are made with `Reference.CreateLinkReference`, present 2020 to 2027. Selecting replaces the selection that was there. **THE LINK IS FOUND BY SELECT_FROM_LINK'S RULES.** A name matching nothing is refused with every link listed, one matching several is AMBIGUOUS and refused, and an unloaded link is said to be unloaded - never answered with a zero. A category list is required: everything in a link includes its levels and grids, and a box round those is the whole site. **NOTHING IS CHANGED, IN THIS MODEL OR IN THE LINK.** No transaction is opened or needed; it moves the camera and, when asked, the selection. So it asks for no confirmation first: a zoom or a selection inside a link is not touching it in Constitution Article 7's sense - the owner's answer to Q-65, D-124.

| **You say** | **link name** - text<br>**categories** - comma separated, resolved BY NAME in Revit; a name matching twice is refused<br>**also select** - yes or no - true or false; optional |
| **You get** | shown, selected, view after, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2020 |
| **Capability** | `ZOOM_TO_LINKED_ELEMENTS` |

**How to use it**

2. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"zoom to the beams in the structural link"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
3. Revit shows the result. Nothing in the model changes.
